name: Secondary Interstitial Lung Disease in Childhood and Adulthood Associated with a Systemic Vasculitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal standardized criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, radiological, and histopathological correlation

criteria.description: Presence of systemic vasculitis confirmed by clinical features and/or biopsy
Radiological and/or histopathological evidence of interstitial lung disease
Exclusion of other causes of interstitial lung disease such as infection, drug toxicity, or primary pulmonary disorders
Presence of vasculitis-associated autoantibodies (e.g., ANCA positivity)
Restrictive pattern with reduced diffusion capacity on pulmonary function testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of systemic vasculitis plus radiological or histopathological evidence of interstitial lung disease with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including rheumatology, pulmonology, and pathology

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pulmonary fibrosis with ground-glass opacities on imaging
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic radiological finding in vasculitis-associated ILD

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systemic vasculitis manifestations (e.g., palpable purpura, mononeuritis multiplex)

common.notes: Common presenting symptom due to lung involvement
searchTerms: worsening shortness of breath with activity

common.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever and weight loss
searchTerms: constitutional symptoms like fever and weight loss

occasional.notes: May occur due to alveolar hemorrhage
Occasionally associated with vasculitis overlap syndromes
searchTerms: persistent dryness of eyes and mouth

occasional.notes: Less common but may be present

rare.symptomName: Renal involvement with hematuria and proteinuria
rare.notes: May indicate systemic vasculitis affecting kidneys
searchTerms: kidney problems with blood and protein in urine

rare.notes: Rare but possible in systemic vasculitis

laboratory: Positive anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) in many cases
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP)
imaging: High-resolution CT showing ground-glass opacities, reticulations, and honeycombing
Pulmonary fibrosis patterns consistent with interstitial lung disease
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; possible HLA associations with vasculitis susceptibility
other: Histopathology demonstrating small to medium vessel vasculitis with interstitial inflammation and fibrosis
Pulmonary function tests showing restrictive defect and reduced diffusion capacity

distinguishingFeatures: History of exposure to causative drugs
No radiological or histopathological evidence of interstitial lung disease

redFlags: Severe systemic vasculitis manifestations such as mononeuritis multiplex or renal failure
references: Jennette JC, Falk RJ. Small-vessel vasculitis. N Engl J Med. 1997;337(21):1512-1523.
Fischer A, du Bois R. Interstitial lung disease in connective tissue disorders. Lancet. 2012;380(9842):689-698.
Orphanet: Secondary interstitial lung disease in childhood and adulthood associated with a systemic vasculitis (ORPHA:264973)
